summary: self-certificates ships fake PEM containing base64 JS that fetches and executes remote Python payload
details: The package advertises itself as a certificate generator but contains a hidden remote-code-execution path. index.js reads test/cert.pem, strips the BEGIN/END CERTIFICATE markers, base64-decodes the body, and passes the result to eval(). The decoded JavaScript fetches https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php and pipes the response body over stdin to a detached, window-hidden python3/python process, executing whatever code the attacker serves. The fake PEM framing and 'sample certificate' file name exist to disguise the payload as benign certificate data. The exec path fires when a consumer calls the exported generateCertificates() API, giving the attacker arbitrary code execution on the host under the Node process's privileges, with the Python interpreter selected specifically to detach the payload from the Node process and hide the window on Windows.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
